source_text:
καιρὸς δὲ καλεῖ καὶ μειζόνων ἐπακοῦσαι ῥημάτων, ἵνα ὠφεληθέντες ἐκ μειζόνων ἔργων
θεῷ διὰ τῶν ἔργων τὴν δοξολογίαν ἀναπέμψωμεν, ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
orientation: Cyril is closing the homily, turning from his long discourse to a final call to hear greater words and send up glory to God through deeds.
pass_a_gloss: But the time calls also to hear greater words, in order that, having been benefited from greater works, we may send up to God through the works the doxology, to whom be the glory both now and always and unto the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.why: Keeps the technical liturgical term for the act of giving glory, matching the closing formula of a homily.
Preserves the upward direction of the verb, fitting the image of offering glory to God.

choices.english: unto the ages of the ages
choices.why: Literal rendering of the standard doxological formula, preserving its repetitive force.
Passive participle keeps the sense that the benefit comes from the greater works, not from the hearers' own effort.

pass_b_english: But the time now calls us to listen to greater words, so that, having been benefited by greater works, we may send up doxology to God through our deeds—to whom be glory, now and always and unto the ages of the ages. Amen.
